question: David bought some sharpeners at the rate of ₹150 a dozen. He sold them for ₹43 each. His profit percentage is ______%.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**CP** of 12 sharpeners = 150

**CP** of 1 sharpener = 150 ÷ 12 = 12.5

**SP** of 1 sharpener = 43

**Profit** per sharpener = 43 − 12.5 = 30.5

**Profit%** = (30.5 ÷ 12.5) × 100 = 244%

**∴ The correct answer is 244%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** CP of 12 items = 150; SP of 1 item = 43.

**Formulas:** Profit = SP − CP | Profit% = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3a7749855528d45b317bbfa50ee387e75c8693abd0a6caeb5d5eb720fa836973.png] 

⇒ **Cost Price (CP)** of 1 unit = 150 ÷ 12 = 12.5

⇒ **Selling Price (SP)** of 1 unit = 43

⇒ **Profit** = 43 − 12.5 = 30.5

⇒ **Profit percentage** = (30.5 ÷ 12.5) × 100

⇒ **Profit percentage** = 2.44 × 100 = 244%

**∴ The correct answer is 244%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Unitary Method in Profit and Loss

Always calculate the **CP** and **SP** for the same quantity (usually 1 unit) to find the profit or loss percentage accurately.

Profit Percentage

Profit% is the **relative gain** over the original Cost Price, expressed as: (Total Profit ÷ Cost Price) × 100.</p
